newsitem.title: CHINA: China soymeal price to fall in late '96 - paper.
newsitem.headline: China soymeal price to fall in late '96 - paper.

text.p: China's soymeal prices, after their recent surge, are expected to fall in the fourth quarter due to imports of soymeal and domestic soybean supplies in the coming months, the Futures Herald said on Monday.

Soymeal prices rose by 1,140 yuan per tonne between May and August, liftiing the spot price to as high as 3,000 yuan per tonne in some parts of the country, including the southeastern province of Fujian and in Heilongjiang in the northeast.
The sharp upturn was atrributed to a 2.1 million tonne fall in the soybean harvest last year and an increase in demand estimated at more than one million tonnes this year.

China imported 500,000-600,000 tonnes of soymeal from India, Mexico, Indonesia and the United States in the first half of this year. Another 500,000 tonnes are on order and should be delivered by the end of this year, the newspaper said.
New soybeans from this year's harvest should be on the market in the autumn, the newspaper said.
Demand for soymeal - used in animal feed - has surged as China's livestock industry grows on the back of increasing meat consumption, driven by higher living standards.
